features.title: Engineering Knowledge Base (document storage, ingestion, hybrid retrieval)
acceptance: workspace-isolated document storage with real RLS, private Supabase Storage
PDF/TXT/Markdown ingestion: extract -> chunk -> embed -> store -> mark indexed, with a PDF with no extractable text marked failed (not silently indexed)
every chunk retains provenance: documentId, filename, page or section, product/revision relationship
searchEngineeringDocuments() does hybrid (keyword + semantic) retrieval via Postgres/pgvector, no separate vector DB
Documents/Sources UI: real counts only, real status (UPLOADING/PROCESSING/INDEXED/FAILED), source preview with highlighted passage
pagination and workspace/product/revision filtering verified against a 120-document programmatic dataset, not just a handful

features.notes: The Investigation Agent (MVP-10B) and citation/source drawer (MVP-10C) are separate follow-on tickets that build on this. The 'semantic' half of retrieval is a zero-dependency local hashed lexical embedding (src/lib/documents/embedding.ts), not a neural embedding model — no embeddings API key is configured, and adding a new third-party credential is a one-way-door decision per CLAUDE.md, not made unasked. Swapping in a real embedding provider later is a drop-in change behind the same EmbeddingAdapter-shaped function signature.

features.title: Investigation Agent (ToolLoopAgent orchestration layer)
acceptance: one Investigation Agent (src/lib/agents), built on AI SDK ToolLoopAgent, with exactly six bounded tools: getProductContext, getMeasurementContext, getDeterministicCorrelations, searchEngineeringDocuments, getPreviousRevisions, getPreviousInvestigations
deterministic correlation (MVP-06) stays guaranteed and unchanged; the agent only runs after real candidates exist, and never recomputes them
structured output only (Zod, via Output.object) — hypotheses[] with reasoning/evidenceRefs/missingEvidence/nextInvestigation, clarificationQuestion, investigationStatus; no free-form prose contract

independent post-hoc validation rejects hallucinated productFactId/certainty language (whole hypothesis) and hallucinated or mismatched document/fact/investigation citations (that one citation only), reusing MVP-07's buildObservedEvidence/buildKnownEvidence/containsProhibitedCertaintyLanguage rather than reimplementing them
bounded tool loop: explicit stopWhen at 9 steps, not the SDK's 20-step default; a model that never produces a final answer fails the run cleanly rather than looping

observable, safe agent.started/agent.tool.completed/agent.completed events (tool name, safe label, result count, durationMs, query) — never hidden reasoning or a raw prompt; persisted and reconstructed exactly like existing analysis_events

truthful agent.completed metrics (documentsAvailable/documentSearches/passagesRetrieved/passagesUsedAsEvidence/deterministicRelationshipsChecked/nextInvestigationCount) computed from real tool-call results, never fabricated
fully backward compatible: createAnalysisRunForFailureCase's agentModel option and runAnalysis's agentRunner are additive/optional — every MVP-08/09 test passes unchanged with neither supplied

live-verified against a real Gateway X case (40 MHz clock, WiFi radio, unshielded display cable, one seeded test-report document, 200 MHz/+7.4dB measurement): full event sequence including 5 document searches, 2 evidence-labeled hypotheses with real document citations (filename+section+exact quoted passage) and no root-cause/certainty language, persisted rows match the stream exactly
features.notes: The polished agent-activity UI (source drawer, live tool-call panel) is MVP-10C, not built here — this ticket is the orchestration layer and its backend event/reducer foundation only. The live test uncovered and fixed two real defects: reasoning/nextInvestigation needed wider Zod bounds (600/300 -> 1200/500 chars) for the agent's evidence-integrated answers, and the tool-activity label pluralizer was naively appending 's' to two-word nouns ('passage retrieveds') — fixed to pluralize the noun only ('passages retrieved'), covered by a regression test.

features.title: Observation updates hypothesis

the previous hypothesis is never rewritten or deleted — a chronological investigation timeline (measurement -> hypothesis -> observation -> updated investigation) proves old and updated hypotheses both remain visible and auditable
refresh reconstructs the observation, updated hypothesis status, and full timeline from persisted rows alone, without rerunning the model
duplicate submission of the observation form is prevented

features.title: Agent-Native Crado Product Experience
acceptance: REAL-TIME AGENTIC FLOW CORRECTION (see docs/PROGRESS.md 'reopened #2' entry): proven root cause of batched activity was runInvestigationAgent collecting agent.tool.completed activity into an in-memory array only readable after the whole multi-step agent.generate() call resolved (live-reproduced: 15.6s frozen, then every remaining step in one ~250ms window) — fixed with investigateStreaming, a callback-to-async-generator bridge yielding each tool completion the instant it happens; run-analysis.ts/create-analysis-run.ts updated to consume it incrementally. Proven root cause of the empty-until-refresh canvas was the fixed origin-anchored defaultViewport never moving again after mount, so a burst of newly-streamed nodes landed outside the still-anchored visible window — fixed with a default-on Follow-agent toggle (setCenter at a fixed readable zoom, never fitBounds/fitView shrinking to fit) that pauses on a real user drag/pan/zoom (xyflow's own event-vs-programmatic onMoveStart convention) and re-enables on click; a graph.nodes.length===0 empty-state placeholder (real lastEventSummary/errorMessage, never fabricated) replaces the previous bare `return null` for an active-but-not-yet-populated run. Live-verified end-to-end twice against the real Gateway X pipeline (real Anthropic model, real Supabase persistence, no mocks): activity progressed across separated timestamps both times, canvas auto-panned to the newest content with no refresh, 3 rapid RUN AGAIN clicks produced exactly one POST, refresh reproduced identical persisted state. 373/373 unit + 61/61 integration tests pass (8 new), lint/typecheck/build clean. Remaining limitation, documented not silently dropped: no server-side cross-tab/cross-client idempotency key.

VISUAL CORRECTION (see docs/PROGRESS.md 'reopened' entry): the investigation canvas's previous top-to-bottom-only layout (build-canvas-graph.ts) produced a narrow, vertically-stretched single chain with excessive empty space and Observation/Next-test card overlap; rewritten into a left-to-right stage/column layout (Measurement -> Deterministic -> Hypothesis -> Missing/Observation -> Next-test -> Change/Revision -> Outcome) with per-hypothesis vertical 'lanes', a two-pass real-DOM-measurement height correction, real zoom/pan Controls (colorMode="dark"), a fixed origin-anchored defaultViewport (no more fitView-on-mount clipping both ends of wide/tall graphs), and a 3-tier responsive breakpoint split (desktop-with-rail / laptop-tablet-canvas-no-rail / mobile-stack, canvas threshold lowered 1024px->768px). Live-verified at 390/768/1024/1280/1440 against real seeded multi-hypothesis Gateway X cases; 365/365 unit + 61/61 integration tests pass, lint/typecheck/build clean.

features.title: Decision-centred investigation workspace
acceptance: PARTIAL — a coherent, fully-verified core slice shipped; several sections of the full ticket are deferred (listed below), so this does not yet meet all 14 acceptance criteria of the source ticket. Baseline preserved unmodified: confirmed HEAD was exactly e6cb8c2 (UX-04 reopened #2) before any edit, all 8 named invariants intact, no AGENTS.md exists anywhere in the repo (confirmed via `find`), no SSE/event-store/persistence rework performed — every new surface consumes the existing WorkspaceState/TimelineEntry projection unmodified.

New default-landing 'Decision' tab (decision-view.tsx) added alongside the existing canvas, now relabeled 'Map' — composes the four already-built-but-dead UX-03 artifact components verbatim (MeasurementPanel, CorrelationCard, HypothesisCard, RevisionComparisonCard) plus one new 'Recommended next test' card sourced entirely from the leading hypothesis's real recommendedNextStep/title (no fabricated structured fields). Sections track real data only: 'What Crado knows'/'Leading hypotheses'/'Recommended next test' each render nothing until the corresponding real correlation/hypothesis exists — never a placeholder implying content that isn't there yet.

src/lib/investigation/rank-hypotheses.ts: deterministic leading/plausible/weakened/unresolved ranking from the run's own real confidenceBand and update.status fields only — no invented percentage or score. src/lib/investigation/derive-workflow-state.ts: truthful workflow-state derivation (awaiting_measurement/idle/analysis_in_progress/analysis_failed/interrupted/more_evidence_needed/ready_for_next_test/change_ready_to_verify/outcome_ready_for_review/resolved) from real RunStatus + timeline engineering_change/result ordering + the failure_cases row's own status — 'resolved' is never inferred from an agent run finishing. AgentStatusPill now reads this instead of a 5-state Complete/Ready/Investigating vocabulary; wired end-to-end through page.tsx's real failureCase.status.

Both Decision and Map now render live from the same WorkspaceState during a run, so the forced tab-switch previously fired on RUN was removed — starting or re-running an investigation no longer yanks the engineer to a specific tab; whichever tab they're on keeps updating in place. Live-verified against a newly created Gateway X investigation (chrome-devtools MCP, no mocks): timestamped polling proved sequential arrival (t=0 activity item, t=4560ms hypothesis appears, t=4711ms run completes with the status pill flipping from 'Agent analysis in progress' to 'Ready for next test', never a bare 'Complete'); Decision and Map were both populated with real content during the run and remained fully populated after completion with no refresh; Map tab (React Flow) showed 5 real nodes post-completion without a reload, reconfirming the UX-04 reopened-#2 fix still holds.
Record result wired: the Decision view's RECORD RESULT button calls the same handleRecordResult the canvas already used, focusing the composer — verified live.

Responsive: 1440/1280/1024/768/390 all live-QA'd on the new Decision tab plus a Map-tab spot check; zero new console errors/warnings at any breakpoint (one pre-existing React Flow attribution dev warning, unrelated to this ticket, noted not a regression).

Tests: derive-workflow-state.test.ts (14 cases incl. boundary — a second engineering change after a result correctly reverts to change_ready_to_verify), rank-hypotheses.test.ts (10 cases), decision-view.test.tsx (7 cases — section presence tracks real data, ranking order, Record result wiring, most-recent-result selection), agent-status-pill.test.tsx (5 cases incl. the 'never bare Complete with open evidence gaps' and 'Resolved only when case record says so' assertions) — 36 new tests, all passing. investigation-workspace.test.tsx's pre-existing 24 tests updated (not weakened) for the new default tab and 'Investigation'->'Map' rename; full suite 408/409 unit tests pass (one case-composer.test.tsx failure is a pre-existing full-run timing flake, confirmed passing 14/14 in isolation, unrelated to any file this ticket touched). typecheck/lint/build all clean.

DEFERRED (not built this ticket, not silently dropped): the Investigations work-queue's four-bucket filters and literal per-row 'required next action' string; a dedicated Before/After comparison screen beyond the Decision view's Outcome section; a dedicated resolved-trajectory narrative view beyond Decision + the existing Timeline tab; Investigation Map minimap/jump-to-active-step control and its own Follow-agent-aware readable-default-zoom tuning pass; a real agent.tool.started durable event (no SDK lifecycle callback for per-tool active state was located this session — the honest overall 'Working…' state plus completed-tool-sequence was retained per the ticket's own explicit instruction, never synthesized client-side); a full WCAG/keyboard-navigation audit across the new Decision surface (basic heading/landmark structure and existing focus/live-region patterns were reused, not independently re-audited); cross-tab/cross-client run-start idempotency remains unenforced server-side, unchanged from UX-04 and explicitly out of scope per this ticket's own text since the run-start boundary was not touched.

CONTINUATION — Workstreams A/B/C shipped in full, D partially (queue filters). A: shadcn Sidebar (src/components/ui/sidebar.tsx) replaces the hand-rolled rail — Cmd/Ctrl+B toggle, collapsed icon mode with real aria-labels, off-canvas mobile Sheet, real destinations only, real open-investigations badge count, real Crado logo assets. B: New investigation now shows a real 'Recent investigations' section (recent-investigations.tsx) — real data ordered by latest activity, restrained generic DeviceGlyph (never a fabricated device icon — schema has no device-category data), truthful workflow state + required next action, one-click resume, loading/empty/error states. C: agent-activity-panel.tsx replaced by investigation-trace-panel.tsx — a real, live Investigation Trace populated by a new agent.tool.started event (additive migration 20260903000000_analysis_events_agent_tool_started.sql), bridged from the AI SDK's real onToolExecutionStart callback in investigateStreaming, threaded through the same canonical persisted-then-streamed SSE pipeline Decision/Map/status already use — a live run and a page-refresh replay produce an identical trace. D (partial): real queue filter buckets (Active/Needs evidence/Ready for review/Resolved) with real counts and a truthful required-next-action string, wired into /investigations via derive-queue-workflow-state.ts (a deliberately lighter, batched-input sibling of derive-workflow-state.ts, proven equivalent by its own 23-case suite).

TWO REAL BUGS FOUND AND FIXED VIA LIVE QA (the significant finding this session): (1) a duplicate React key crash — investigation-agent.ts was keying tool-call events by the AI SDK's event.callId, which the SDK documents as the *generation call's* id, shared by every tool executed within one model step (proven live: 5 tools called together in one step all shared one callId); fixed by using the real per-call event.toolCall.toolCallId instead, verified against real Anthropic toolu_... ids in analysis_events post-fix, plus a regression test scripting a multi-tool-in-one-step model turn and a defensive dedup-by-key backstop in investigation-trace-panel.tsx's buildSteps. (2) Immediately after fixing (1), a live run crashed with a real React 'Maximum update depth exceeded' — useElapsedTime's getSnapshot computed Date.now()-startedAt directly, violating useSyncExternalStore's contract that getSnapshot return a stable value between actual store changes; fixed by caching the elapsed value in a ref written once per interval tick. Both fully re-verified live end-to-end afterward: correct elapsed timer, 6 real tool steps streamed with correct per-call durations, truthful completion status, zero console errors, identical persisted-trace reconstruction on refresh.

Tests: app-shell-chrome.test.tsx (10), device-glyph.test.tsx (4), derive-queue-workflow-state.test.ts (23), recent-investigations.test.tsx (6), investigation-trace-panel.test.tsx (14, incl. the duplicate-key regression) all new; investigation-agent.test.ts, run-analysis.test.ts, reconstruct.test.ts, investigation-workspace.test.tsx, describe-investigation-status.test.ts, create-analysis-run.integration.test.ts updated. Full unit suite 464/464 (57 files), run 3 times consecutively, all green — the previously documented case-composer.test.tsx full-suite-only flake did not reproduce across any of the 3 runs and was left unmodified (nothing reproducible to fix). Integration suite 62/62 (12 files). typecheck/lint/build all clean.

Live QA (chrome-devtools MCP, real Anthropic calls, no mocks): a brand-new investigation with zero product facts correctly produced 'no investigation hypotheses were generated' and never ran the agent phase (confirmed via analysis_events — the deterministic-correlation gate working as documented, not a bug); a RUN AGAIN on an existing case with a real 40 MHz clock product fact was used to reproduce and re-verify both bugs above end-to-end; Sidebar/New investigation/queue filters re-screenshotted with real data and zero console errors; breakpoints 1440/1024/768/390 swept on Trace/Decision surfaces, clean reflow, zero console errors (one pre-existing, unrelated cosmetic mobile composer-label clip noted, not a regression from this session).

STILL DEFERRED after this continuation, in dependency order for a future session: dedicated Before/After comparison screen; dedicated resolved-trajectory narrative view (independent of Before/After); Investigation Map minimap/jump-to-active-step control; a full WCAG/keyboard-navigation audit across all new surfaces (best done last, once every surface it needs to cover exists). Cross-tab/cross-client run-start idempotency remains unenforced server-side, unchanged from UX-04, still out of scope. UX-04/UX-04-LIGHT remain untouched.

features.title: Enterprise authentication redesign
acceptance: Sign in (/login) and Sign up (/signup, new route) rebuilt as a shared two-region shell (src/lib/design/auth-shell.tsx) — restrained Crado context pane + card-free auth pane — replacing the old floating premium card. No generic SaaS template, glass card, gradient hero, or fabricated SSO. Only real configured auth methods shown: Supabase email+password only, verified via supabase/config.toml (every [auth.external.*] provider disabled).

src/lib/auth/actions.ts (moved from src/app/login/actions.ts, shared by both pages) keeps the exact same signInWithPassword/signUp calls, session-presence check and credentialsSchema — auth provider, credential strategy and session model unchanged. Honest, non-enumerating error mapping (src/lib/auth/map-auth-error.ts) branches only on real Supabase AuthError.status/.code/.name values (rate limit, retryable network failure, unconfirmed email, weak password); sign-in's invalid-credentials and sign-up's collision case each keep one generic message deliberately, matching Supabase's own anti-enumeration behavior.

sanitizeRedirectTarget (src/lib/auth/redirect.ts) now guards every next value reaching redirect() — the proxy's own redirect, both forms' hidden next field, and /auth/confirm's query string (previously passed through unsanitized, a real open-redirect-shaped gap, fixed as a scoped defect fix). Both pages are Server Components that redirect an already-authenticated visitor to the sanitized next before rendering the form (previously they did not).

Two real, previously-silent gaps fixed: middleware.ts's own next query param was never read by the old /login page, and /auth/confirm's ?error=confirmation-failed was never displayed — both now surface as real, honest UI (a page-level notice banner). A new expired=1 signal (hasSupabaseAuthCookie in middleware.ts, checked before getUser()) distinguishes a genuinely stale session from a visitor who was never signed in, shown as 'Your session has expired.'

REAL DEFECT FOUND AND FIXED VIA LIVE QA: React 19 resets a form's uncontrolled fields once its useActionState action settles, silently clearing the typed email on every server-side error — caught by live-typing real credentials into a running dev server and watching the field go blank, not anticipated in advance. Fixed by tracking email as real component state (password deliberately stays uncontrolled/cleared) in both sign-in-form.tsx and sign-up-form.tsx; reproduced as a regression test in both files' test suites.

Password visibility toggle (src/lib/design/password-input.tsx) is genuinely keyboard-operable — live-verified via a real Tab+Enter sequence in the browser (not just a click), aria-pressed reflects state, accessible name states the action taken. Fields limited to exactly what the schema needs: no name/company/phone on sign-up, no password-confirmation field, no fabricated forgot-password link on sign-in (no reset flow exists in the codebase).

Absent flows deliberately not fabricated, recorded in docs/PROGRESS.md rather than built or silently skipped: forgot-password/password-reset, email-verification resend, workspace invitations, OAuth/SSO/magic-link sign-in, Privacy Policy/Terms of Service links (no such routes exist in the repo).

Tests: redirect.test.ts (9), map-auth-error.test.ts (7), middleware.test.ts (5, first test in this repo to mock @supabase/ssr), sign-in-form.test.tsx (7), sign-up-form.test.tsx (6) — all new. Full unit suite 521/521 across 65 files. tsc/lint/production build all clean; /signup appears as its own dynamic route in the build output.

Live QA (chrome-devtools MCP, real running dev server, real local Supabase, no mocks) signed out by clearing the real sb-127-auth-token cookie: 1440/1280/768/390 in both themes for both pages, zero console errors/warnings at any breakpoint (one next/image Preflight-height warning found and fixed during the pass), no horizontal overflow, no clipped footer/action. Real incorrect-credentials error, real successful sign-up end-to-end (workspace auto-created by the existing handle_new_user DB trigger, confirmed truthful), real duplicate-email attempt (non-enumerating), real expired-session banner, real invalid-confirmation-link banner, already-authenticated redirect, and full next-param round-trip across the Sign in <-> Sign up switch links all verified against real behavior, not mocked. A throwaway QA signup account (crado-auth-qa@example.com) was created to prove the flow end-to-end, then deleted via the Supabase admin API afterward, per CLAUDE.md's 'do not create unnecessary production users' and 'clear deletion path for pilot data.'

DEFERRED, per this ticket's own explicit 'do not start' instruction: Evidence/Timeline/Map flat-workbench adaptation and homepage restructuring (both remain UX-05's own remaining scope, untouched this session). Also noted, not confirmed: the sidebar's existing 'Sign out' menu item did not reliably submit via CDP's synthetic click during QA (worked around by clearing the cookie directly) — signOut itself was not modified (out of scope: global shell, not auth pages), flagged as a possible real UI defect worth a future look.

features.title: Decision view, answer-first layout
acceptance: Decision is now the page, not one tab of five: view-switcher.tsx and investigation-item-table.tsx deleted outright (confirmed via grep before deletion — investigation-item-table.tsx had exactly one real importer, decision-view.tsx, and no dedicated test file; view-switcher.tsx had zero remaining importers once investigation-workspace.tsx stopped using it). investigation-workspace.tsx's InvestigationTab five-way type/state and its 40-44px toolbar row are gone, replaced by a two-value MainView = "decision" | "map" local toggle. Evidence/History(Timeline)/Sources became closed-by-default AdvancedDisclosure rows inside decision-view.tsx, reusing EvidenceView/InvestigationTimeline/SourcesPanel verbatim (not rebuilt) — each gated on real data (hypotheses.length>0 / timeline.length>0 / agentMetrics!==null) so an empty section renders nothing rather than an empty disclosure.

InvestigationItemTable's shared <table> retired for the reason recorded here verbatim, not by omission: arithmetic and machine guesses must not be rendered as siblings in one table. reasoning-section.tsx (new) composes CorrelationCard(s) left / ranked HypothesisCard(s) right in a grid gap-4 lg:grid-cols-2, each its own <article>/<div>, never a shared table row. Condition C decisions made deliberately, not by omission: 'State' (Verified — deterministic check / the real Leading-Plausible-Weakened-Unresolved rank) now lives directly on each card via a new optional isSelected/strength prop set on CorrelationCard and HypothesisCard; 'Updated by' (Deterministic check vs Agent) was deliberately dropped — once the two objects are their own visually distinct kind, which one produced a row is no longer information a reader needs restated.

Condition B (visual distinguishability, checked not assumed): live-verified in the browser, both themes — the deterministic card renders a plain monospace equation (`40 MHz × 5 = 200 MHz`) with a neutral/indigo left accent and no color-coded sections; the hypothesis card carries an orange left accent, an orange ⚠ 'HYPOTHESIS N · INFERRED' label, and orange-marked OBSERVED/KNOWN/INFERRED/MISSING section bullets. Honest answer: yes, distinguishable at a glance even with labels covered — different accent color, different typography (monospace numerals vs prose), different iconography, not just a different heading string.

Failure summary is one prose sentence (failure-strip.tsx rewritten): '{freq} MHz measured {margin} dB above/below the selected limit, with {mode} active.' plus a second line (test type · revision · measured-when · Add measurement). The stored spectrum plot (single peak + limit line, no real trace) was removed from this surface per the approved Decision Sheet — rendering it at legible size here would restate two numbers the sentence already gives, and at thumbnail size it would be illegible, which the ticket explicitly forbids anywhere. It was relocated instead of deleted: SpectrumChart now renders inside ContextRail's MeasurementDetail, so it's still reachable, just not on the answer-first path.

Recommended next test is the largest, most prominent block (next-action-bar.tsx restyled, not restructured): promoted to a bordered/accented card with text-xl/2xl leading-snug recommendation text and no truncate class anywhere in its render path — live-verified at 1440px on a completed seeded case (Gateway X CASE-4FA53E) with a 4-line recommendation rendering in full, no scroll, no ellipsis. Also verified at 1280/1024/768/390 in both themes: full text intact at every breakpoint, single-column reflow below 1024px, header wraps to two lines by 768px without truncating any of product/revision/case-ref/status.

'View as map' toggle placed adjacent to the Reasoning heading (reasoning-section.tsx), not in the header — the header (top-bar.tsx call site) now carries only product/revision/case-ref/status/Run again, with the prior duplicated 'Radiated emissions — {product} {revision}' backLabel replaced by the plain literal 'Back to case' (criterion 1). Live-verified: clicking it renders the existing InvestigationCanvas full-width with a 'Back to decision' return button; the composer stays docked at the exact same position in the main column across the toggle in both directions (verified by screenshot comparison, not inferred).

Trace pane is unmountable, not just visually hidden, when a run is not active — confirmed via accessibility-tree query (queryByText/queryByRole, not toBeVisible) in both the new investigation-workspace.test.tsx assertions and live browser DOM inspection. A live run (chrome-devtools MCP, real Anthropic calls, real seeded case) was started and screenshotted mid-run at 1440px: the Trace pane renders as a genuine separate left ResizablePanel (live checkmarked steps, 'Working…' status) beside the Main column, not stacked inline — confirming the desktop 3-pane split is real, not simulated. Once the run completed, the Trace panel unmounted and its content reappeared inside Decision's own 'What Crado checked · N checks · Xs' disclosure (verified fully expanded: itemized trace list + AgentMetricsPanel's 'What Crado handled' grid, both matching the completed run's real numbers).

Composer relocation confirmed stable across a run's full start-to-end transition, live: the same <form> instance (same docked position, bottom of the Main column, full width) was present before the run started, mid-run (beside the now-mounted Trace pane), and after the run completed (Trace unmounted) — it never moved, because it was deliberately relocated out of the old Trace-pane footer into a shared renderMainColumn() footer used identically by all three responsive branches (this is the forced architectural consequence of the Trace pane becoming conditionally unmountable, not a layout tweak — see docs/PROGRESS.md's UX-07 entry).

Agent metrics (tools used/model steps/sources cited) are not visible on first paint of a completed case — live-verified: 'What Crado checked' starts closed, showing only the real computed summary line ('7 checks · 16.6s'); clicking it reveals the full AgentMetricsPanel grid. No hypothesis title, no recommended-next-test text, and no case-header segment was found truncated at 1440/1280/1024/768/390 in either theme during live QA.

Condition A (real test impact, counted before editing, not assumed): decision-view.test.tsx fully rewritten, 6 → 11 tests; investigation-workspace.test.tsx had 16 of its existing test cases edited (10 mechanical {name:"Map"}→{name:"View as map"} renames, 6 substantively rewritten for the new disclosure/trace-lifecycle behavior, plus 2 new tests added) — a real count materially higher than the Decision Sheet's original 'two test rewrites' estimate, exactly as flagged. Every rewritten assertion still fails if the underlying guarantee breaks (e.g. the 'never duplicates the trace' test asserts the trace is either exactly-1-present or fully-absent depending on state, not merely 'present somewhere'; the not-truncated test asserts the className, not just visible text). Full suite: 527/527 unit (65 files), 62/62 integration (12 files), tsc/lint/build all clean.

Not met / deliberately out of scope: the composer's placeholder text visually clips against the SEND button at the 768px and 390px breakpoints — a pre-existing case-composer.tsx behavior, unmodified by this ticket (that file was never touched) and left as-is rather than fixed under a layout-only ticket's scope boundary. No other acceptance criterion was found unmet during live QA.

CORRECTION (rejected on review — layout order was right, rendering was not): three real content-assembly bugs fixed, not evidence-model changes. (1) Duplicate KNOWN evidence line — validateAgentOutput pushed a hypothesis's grounding fact into evidence once via its own correlation candidate, then again whenever the model's evidenceRefs cited that same fact by id; fixed with a new dedupeEvidence helper (generate-hypotheses.ts, by category+description), applied in both validateAgentOutput and generateHypothesesForMeasurement, with a unit test (two identical inputs -> one output) plus a validateAgentOutput regression reproducing the exact duplicate scenario. Live-verified: the case's pre-existing persisted hypothesis still shows the old duplicate (fixing assembly code doesn't retroactively rewrite stored rows — correct), but a freshly triggered run produced the KNOWN fact exactly once. (2) 'Why this test' removed entirely from hypothesis-card.tsx — it always reprinted the hypothesis's own INFERRED paragraph verbatim, a second copy of text already shown above it. (3) The recommended next test no longer renders inside the hypothesis card at all — it duplicated next-action-bar.tsx's own pinned copy; the pinned bar is now the page's single home for the recommended action, asserted via getAllByText(...).toHaveLength(1) in decision-view.test.tsx.

CORRECTION — fixed type scale applied literally per the ticket's own 'apply exactly, do not interpret' instruction (new reasoning-typography.ts): card title 15px/500/1.4, body/evidence text 13px/400/1.55, section labels and eyebrow 11px/500/uppercase/0.06em, technical values (frequencies, dB, equations) 13px monospace, next-test text 14px/400 — a deliberate step down from the first pass's oversized equation (text-2xl/3xl) and headline-sized recommendation (text-xl/2xl). The failure-strip's peak/margin sentence was deliberately left untouched, per the ticket's own named exception, rather than split mid-sentence into two sizes.

CORRECTION — decoration removed: the ●◆△○ per-category glyphs, the colored left border per evidence section, and the PLAUSIBLE/MEDIUM CONFIDENCE/candidate-relationship pill badges are gone from hypothesis-card.tsx and correlation-card.tsx. Each card keeps exactly one border (its own 2px outer accent) — nothing nested inside it is its own bordered/background box (the old NEXT INVESTIGATION nested-box pattern is gone along with bug 3 above). Confidence/strength/update-status and 'Candidate relationship' are now plain uppercase text folded into each card's eyebrow line. Italic removed from the INFERRED paragraph.

CORRECTION — evidence restructured as a two-column definition list (fixed 96px label column, 8px row spacing, 16px section spacing, 16px card padding, all literal per the ticket) with a new ClampedText component (2-line clamp for OBSERVED/KNOWN/INFERRED, 1-line for MISSING, character-length heuristic deliberately chosen over a ResizeObserver-based real layout measurement so the expand/collapse behavior stays genuinely testable in jsdom). Hypothesis card caps at max-h-[320px] (verified live via getBoundingClientRect() -- exactly 320px at both 1440 and 1024 on a card with enough evidence to need it); header/title stay always visible, the evidence list scrolls internally for overflow rather than clipping or growing the card. Buttons: one primary style, one secondary, both sentence case, 13px/32px (record-engineering-change-form.tsx's trigger button previously rendered already-sentence-case text through an uppercase CSS transform -- removing the transform, not the text, fixed the mixed-case look). Overflow/clipping (acceptance criterion 2, explicitly failing before this pass): shrinking the recommendation text to 14px removed the size pressure that caused it; min-w-0/break-words added defensively throughout.

CORRECTION verification: pnpm run lint / tsc --noEmit / build all clean. Unit suite 531/531 (four new: three dedupeEvidence cases plus one validateAgentOutput regression). Integration 62/62. Tests rewritten to the same standard as this ticket's own original condition A (a moved assertion must still fail if the guarantee breaks) -- hypothesis-card.test.tsx's old 'reuses INFERRED reasoning as why this test' test replaced with its exact opposite (neither Next investigation nor Why this test render; the INFERRED paragraph appears exactly once). Live QA (chrome-devtools MCP, real seeded Gateway X case, no mocks): a genuine before/after pair captured by git-stashing this correction's changes, reloading to screenshot the real pre-fix render, then popping the stash and confirming the tree matched the already-taken post-fix screenshots -- sent to the user as files. 1440 (dark+light)/1280/1024/768/390 all swept; a fresh live run (not the case's pre-existing persisted hypothesis) confirmed bug 1's fix applies to newly-generated evidence. Human gate answered honestly: yes -- on the fresh run's rendering, the failing frequency, calculated relationship, leading hypothesis title, and full recommended-next-test text are all visible together at 1440px with no scrolling and nothing expanded; clamped 'Show more' controls only ever hide supporting detail, never those four facts. Not fixed, out of scope, noted plainly: the composer's placeholder still clips against SEND at 768/390 (case-composer.tsx, untouched by this ticket).

features.title: Hypothesis card, remaining corrections
acceptance: Baseline check performed, not assumed: PR #1 (ux-07-decision-answer-first-layout) had already merged before this ticket's own fixup commit (a5b8fda) was pushed — confirmed via gh pr view 1 (mergedAt 05:09:55Z vs the commit's 06:41:03Z push) and git log origin/main..origin/<branch> showing the commit absent from main. This, not a dedupe-keying bug, is why item 1's duplicate KNOWN line was still visible in production. Recovered by cherry-picking a5b8fda cleanly onto a fresh branch (ux-08-hypothesis-card-corrections) cut from a freshly-pulled origin/main.

Item 1 (duplicate KNOWN line) re-verified against a freshly triggered run on the real seeded case after the cherry-pick: KNOWN section now shows the fact exactly once. The existing dedupeEvidence() keys on category+description (the rendered fields), not an id, so the ticket's suspected root cause did not apply once the fix actually reached main.

Item 2 (coloured card borders) — new for this ticket: removed the one remaining border-l-2 accent bar from both hypothesis-card.tsx (was border-l-warning/amber) and correlation-card.tsx (was border-l-muted-foreground, extended for consistency though not literally named). Both cards now carry only surface.card's own uniform border-border on all four sides; distinguished by eyebrow text and internal structure, never by border colour. Verified with a genuine git-stash before/after screenshot pair at 1440/1280, both themes, against a freshly generated hypothesis.

Items 3/4/5/6/7 (glyphs, pills, non-token colour, italic, single-column evidence order) were already satisfied by the cherry-picked UX-07-correction code — re-verified directly by grep (no ●◆△○, no amber/warning class, no hardcoded hex, no italic class, OBSERVED/KNOWN/INFERRED/MISSING already in a single ordered dl) rather than assumed carried over.

New regression tests (2 per card, 4 total): assert no border-l-* class on the outer container, and assert no amber/warning class fragment, no hardcoded hex, no glyph character, and (correlation card) no rounded-full pill on 'Candidate relationship' anywhere in the rendered HTML. Sanity-checked as real coverage via git stash --keep-index: reverting only the two component files made exactly these new assertions fail; restoring the fix made all 16 tests in the two files pass again.

No hosted deployment exists for this pilot yet (verified via Vercel MCP: zero projects under the linked team; matches MVP-16's own passes:false) — disclosed rather than fabricated; live QA was performed against the real local dev server instead, same seeded case, no mocks.

Legibility question answered from an actual screenshot, not inferred from code: yes, OBSERVED is still distinguishable from INFERRED at a glance with all colour removed — each label sits in a fixed 96px left column, uppercase, one per row, and the four words themselves plus consistent row position carry the distinction. No follow-up weight/spacing change needed.

pnpm run lint / pnpm exec tsc --noEmit clean; hypothesis-card.test.tsx + correlation-card.test.tsx: 16/16 passing directly. See docs/PROGRESS.md's UX-08 entry for the full root-cause writeup, the cherry-pick recovery, and the before/after screenshot verification.
